payload.name: Mere Ownership Effect
payload.fact: The mere ownership effect, where object preference changes following an ownership manipulation, is predicted by activity in the medial prefrontal cortex (MPFC).
payload.boundary: The effect is contingent on the importance of the owned object's functional attribute to the self, particularly when the self-concept is threatened.

provenance.title: I own therefore I can: Efficacy-based mere ownership effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: Recent research found that mere ownership could also affect one's evaluation of domain specific self-efficacy, such as perceiving the self as having greater efficacy when experiencing mere ownership (vs. without-ownership) of an object

provenance.title: I own therefore I can: Efficacy-based mere ownership effect
provenance.quote_or_locus: We demonstrated that efficacy-based mere ownership effect occurred only when the self-concept was threatened (vs. not threatened) (Study 1), and when the attributes of the owned object was central (vs. not central) to the idiosyncratic self-concept (Study 2), or culturally-derived self-concept (Study 3

provenance.title: On the social nature of nonsocial perception: The mere ownership effect.
provenance.quote_or_locus: Study 1 confirmed the existence of this mere ownership effect

provenance.title: Extended self: spontaneous activation of medial prefrontal cortex by objects that are ‘mine’
provenance.quote_or_locus: In addition, change in object preference following the ownership manipulation (a mere ownership effect) was predicted by activity in MPFC
